newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends quietly steady.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends quietly steady.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended steady after drifting narrowly, aided by gains in overseas markets and year-end covering, dealers said.

RSS grades rebounded slightly in the afternoon following gains in Tokyo, with January RSS 1 buyer closing steady at Monday's 315.50 cents ($1.24) a kg after falling earlier. January SMR 20 buyer was up a cent at 305.50 cents.

"Prices did not move a lot today. There was hardly much demand except for some interest from South Korea and few European consumers who need to cover for their year-end," a dealer at a trading firm said.
Dealers said SMR CV was offered at 362 cents for January, SMR L at 342 cents, SMR 5 at 317, SMR 10 at 306 and drum latex at 235.
"Supply is a bit tight because of the wet spell and producers are holding back some of their stocks," the dealer said.
The INRO five-day moving average was 240.76 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 9 from 241.20 on Dec 6. The daily indicator price was 239.91 against 240.15.
